hints: Identify the angles: the upper string pulls upwards and towards the wall ($60^\circ$ to vertical), the lower string pulls downwards and towards the wall ($60^\circ$ to vertical), and the horizontal force $X = 100\text{ N}$ pulls away from the wall.
Resolve vertically: $T_U\cos 60^\circ - T_L\cos 60^\circ - mg = 0$, giving $T_U - T_L = 100\text{ N}$.
Subtract the two relations to solve for the tension in the lower string $T_L$.
walkthrough:
Resolve vertically in equilibrium with $m = 5\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T_U\cos 60^\circ - T_L\cos 60^\circ - 5(10) = 0$$
$$(T_U - T_L)(0.5) = 50 \implies T_U - T_L = 100\text{ N}$$

Resolve horizontally in equilibrium with $X = 100\text{ N}$:
$$100 - T_U\sin 60^\circ - T_L\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$(T_U + T_L)\sin 60^\circ = 100$$
$$T_U + T_L = \frac{100}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \frac{200}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 115.470\text{ N}$$

Subtract the vertical difference equation from the horizontal sum equation:
$$2T_L = 115.470 - 100 = 15.470$$
$$T_L = \frac{15.470}{2} \approx 7.74\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Set up a Cartesian coordinate system with the horizontal direction away from the wall as $+x$ and the upward vertical direction as $+y$.

Identify the forces acting on the $5\text{ kg}$ block:
- Applied horizontal force: $X = 100\text{ N}$ in $+x$-direction.
- Upper string tension $T_U$: directed at $60^\circ$ to the vertical, so component in $-x$ is $T_U\sin 60^\circ$ and component in $+y$ is $T_U\cos 60^\circ$.
- Lower string tension $T_L$: directed at $60^\circ$ to the vertical, so component in $-x$ is $T_L\sin 60^\circ$ and component in $-y$ is $T_L\cos 60^\circ$.
- Downward gravitational force: $W = mg = (5)(10) = 50\text{ N}$.

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$
$$T_U\cos 60^\circ - T_L\cos 60^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$(T_U - T_L)(0.5) = 50$$
Multiply both sides by $2$:
$$T_U - T_L = 100\quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\sum F_x = 0$$
$$100 - T_U\sin 60^\circ - T_L\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$(T_U + T_L)\sin 60^\circ = 100$$
Substitute $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$T_U + T_L = \frac{200}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 115.470\text{ N}\quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2 to eliminate $T_U$:
$$(T_U + T_L) - (T_U - T_L) = 115.470 - 100$$
$$2T_L = 15.470$$
Divide by $2$:
$$T_L = \frac{15.470}{2} \approx 7.735\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$T_L = 7.74\text{ N}$$
Thus the tension in the lower string is $7.74\text{ N}$.

hints: For the block to remain in equilibrium in the given position, both strings must remain taut, meaning $T_L \ge 0$.
The least value of $X$ occurs at the critical boundary where the lower string becomes slack: $T_L = 0$.
Set $T_L = 0$ in the vertical equilibrium equation to find $T_U$, then substitute into the horizontal equation to determine $X$.
walkthrough:
Set the tension in the lower string to zero for the least value of $X$:
$$T_L = 0$$

Resolve vertically with $T_L = 0$:
$$T_U\cos 60^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$T_U(0.5) = 50 \implies T_U = 100\text{ N}$$

Resolve horizontally to find the least value of $X$:
$$X - T_U\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$X = 100\sin 60^\circ = 100\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50\sqrt{3} \approx 86.6\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Physical condition for least $X$: for the block to maintain the geometry shown, the strings must not be pushed into compression (strings can only pull, $T \ge 0$). As horizontal pulling force $X$ decreases, the tension $T_L$ in the lower string decreases until it reaches zero ($T_L = 0$). Any further decrease in $X$ would cause the block to swing inwards, collapsing the geometry.

Set $T_L = 0$ in the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$T_U\cos 60^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$T_U(0.5) = 50$$
$$T_U = \frac{50}{0.5} = 100\text{ N}$$

Substitute $T_U = 100\text{ N}$ into the horizontal equilibrium equation:
$$X - T_U\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$X = T_U\sin 60^\circ = 100\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Evaluate numerically:
$$X = 50(1.73205) \approx 86.6025\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$X = 86.6\text{ N}$$
Thus the least value of $X$ is $86.6\text{ N}$ (or $50\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$).
